title: MECP2 MBD-ID Module: A Unified DNA/RNA Binding Interface Disrupted in Rett Syndrome
authors: Josiah A. Peter; Thomas A. Weiser; Robert T. Batey; Lee A. Niswander; Deborah S. Wuttke
one_liner_zh: 该文研究MECP2的MBD-ID模块作为DNA/RNA结合界面，通过实验揭示其协同结合机制，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作但以湿实验为主，缺乏AI或物理模拟方法，对TF-DNA建模借鉴有限。
abstract: Rett syndrome neurodevelopmental disorder is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the epigenetic regulator MECP2. While the MECP2 methyl-CpG binding domain (MBD) is well-characterized, the function of the adjacent intervening domain (ID) remains largely understudied. The ID has been described as a distinct RNA-binding region, yet evidence also suggests RNA competitively displaces MECP2 from DNA. Here, we address these conflicting findings by demonstrating the MBD and ID do not function in isolation but as a synergistic functional unit, establishing a new model for MECP2 function. We show the ID significantly enhances affinity of the MBD for methylated DNA by ∼35-fold. Moreover, together these two subdomains form a high-affinity, promiscuous RNA-binding module, with affinity for structured RNAs increased over 1,000-fold compared to the MBD or ID alone. We find binding to RNA precludes binding to DNA, such that the integrated MBD-ID unit explains the competition phenomenon. Analysis of Rett syndrome-associated ID mutations (R167W, K174Q, and R190H) and a therapeutic MiniGene reveals they do not disrupt methyl-DNA binding but instead selectively weaken RNA and non-methylated DNA binding, thereby disrupting the competitive balance between nucleic acid ligands. Our work establishes the MBD-ID module as MECP2’s central nucleic acid interaction hub, whose disruption provides a potential molecular etiology of Rett syndrome due to mutations in the intervening domain. GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT
abstract_zh: Rett综合征神经发育障碍由编码表观遗传调控因子MECP2的基因突变引起。虽然MECP2的甲基-CpG结合域（MBD）已被充分表征，但相邻的间隔域（ID）的功能在很大程度上仍未得到充分研究。ID曾被描述为一个独特的RNA结合区域，然而也有证据表明RNA能竞争性地将MECP2从DNA上置换下来。在此，我们通过证明MBD和ID并非孤立发挥作用，而是作为一个协同功能单元，解决了这些相互矛盾的发现，为MECP2功能建立了新模型。我们显示，ID显著增强了MBD对甲基化DNA的亲和力，约提高35倍。此外，这两个子域共同形成一个高亲和力、混杂的RNA结合模块，其对结构化RNA的亲和力相比单独的MBD或ID增加了超过1000倍。我们发现，与RNA的结合会阻止与DNA的结合，因此整合的MBD-ID单元解释了这一竞争现象。对Rett综合征相关ID突变（R167W、K174Q和R190H）及一种治疗性MiniGene的分析显示，它们并不破坏甲基-DNA结合，而是选择性地削弱RNA和非甲基化DNA的结合，从而破坏核酸配体之间的竞争平衡。我们的工作确立了MBD-ID模块作为MECP2的核心核酸相互作用枢纽，其破坏为间隔域突变导致Rett综合征提供了潜在的分子病因学解释。图形摘要
